name: The Gravity Problem: Why SNT Must Be Made in Space
author: Meridian Orbital Dynamics, BioManufacturing Division
body:
Synthetic Neurovascular Tissue cannot be manufactured on Earth. This is not a trade secret or an artificial scarcity — it is physics.

SNT cell cultures require microgravity to form the three-dimensional vascular and neural networks that give the material its integration properties. In standard gravity, the cells settle into flat layers. In microgravity, they grow into the complex, interconnected structures that allow simultaneous vascular, neural, and structural bonding.

Specifically, the critical phase of SNT manufacturing — the 72-hour neural mesh formation window — requires gravitational acceleration below 10⁻⁴ g. This level of microgravity is only achievable in orbital facilities. Attempts to replicate the conditions using centrifuge compensation, magnetic levitation, and acoustic suspension have all failed. The cells know the difference.

All commercial SNT is manufactured at the Ascension Tether's counterweight station at 104,000 km altitude. Three production modules operate continuously, producing approximately 4,000 square meters of SNT per month. This output serves the entire planet.

The implications are significant:
— Every cybernetic implant on Earth depends on material manufactured in orbit
— Meridian Orbital Dynamics controls physical access to the only facility capable of producing SNT
— The three licensed SNT producers pay Meridian approximately Φ200 billion per year in facility lease and logistics fees
— Any disruption to the Ascension Tether would halt SNT production globally within 6 months (current strategic reserve)

The orbital manufacturing monopoly is the primary reason SNT remains expensive, and by extension, why quality cyberware remains inaccessible to Tier 1-2 economic strata without debt financing, insurance coverage, or black-market alternatives.

Meridian Orbital Dynamics has stated publicly that they 'welcome competition in orbital biomanufacturing' and would 'happily lease additional production space to qualified manufacturers.' No qualified manufacturer has the capital to build a competing orbital facility. The Ascension Tether is the only space elevator. Rocket-based logistics cannot compete on cost. The monopoly is structural and permanent.
